caption_content_paraphrase: Earlier attempts were efforts of single scholars; a team effort with different expertise is proposed.
Regional corpora not yet attempted but feasible, giving statistics a sounder footing; so far the corpus has been treated as one block with no chronological or geographical split.

Inventory by site size (over 500, 100-200, 20-50 signs) could be investigated further in the context of use at 29:00-29:15; sign 740 at 10% of occurrences, top three 20%, top six 30%, top twenty half at 29:20-29:50, reported as a finding; much work could be done on the system at 30:00.

Inscriptions outside the valley were analysed from Parpola in the 1980s and found to convey non-canonical sequences; one example seal; frequent man and twins signs read by some as patronymics and by others as another language. No request to study.

Unbalanced oligopoly defined; unicorn, and the Indus bison outside the valley, as the majority component; same iconographies at the same frequencies for almost a millennium; seals compared with corporate ID badges and guild symbols.
Probably rejected any influence from other scripts and did not need other uses of writing such as longer texts or narratives. The other cited windows were not re-read.
Script called an original invention rooted around the turn from the fourth to the third millennium (the caption wording is garbled). The 17:05-24:00 window was not re-read.
